title: Pekudei: in all their journeys (Exodus 40:38)
hookLine: Exodus ends with cloud by day and fire by night, traveling with them
carry: cloud by day, fire by night

lines: HOW DO YOU KNOW WHEN TO MOVE?
THE BOOK ENDS ON THE ROAD.
cards: How do you know when it's time to move? Change jobs, leave a city, end something, start something. A sign would help: something clear, outside your own head, that says go now, or stay put.

The Israelites in the desert had one. Over the sanctuary hung a cloud, and they watched it. The last three verses of Exodus tell how it worked, and they don't end the book with a speech or a battle or a death.
They end it on the road.

teach.h: WHEN THE CLOUD LIFTED, THEY WENT.
teach.b: When the cloud lifted from the sanctuary, the people packed up and traveled. When it didn't lift, they stayed, however long it rested.

teach.h: SEEN BY ALL THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL.
teach.b: Then the last verse of the book, in the JPS 1917 translation: "For the cloud of the LORD was upon the tabernacle by day, and there was fire therein by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys."

Cloud by day, fire by night, seen by everyone: not a private sign for Moses, but a guide the whole people could look up and see. Rashi notices something small in those last words, throughout all their journeys.
The verse is talking about the cloud resting on the tent, which happens when they're camped, not when they're moving. So why call it their journeys?

teach.h: EVERY STOP IS PART OF THE JOURNEY.
teach.b: Rashi's answer: every place they camped is also called a journey, because from each stop, they set out again. The resting places are part of the trip.

teach.h: FROM SLAVERY TO THE OPEN ROAD.
teach.b: Look back at where this book began: in Egypt, building store cities for Pharaoh, in a house of slavery. The book called in Hebrew Shemot, names, began with the names of a family going down into Egypt.

teach.h: CLOUD BY DAY, FIRE BY NIGHT.
teach.b: It ends in the open desert, with a whole people on the move, a home for God in the middle of the camp, and the cloud of the LORD over them in all their journeys.

how: The closing verses of Exodus are chanted in synagogue at the end of Pekudei, and the cloud and fire guiding the camp are described again in more detail in Numbers 9.

games.q: you're in the camp. the cloud has rested on the sanctuary for a month, and you're itching to move on. what do the people do?
o: pack up and go ahead without it.
send scouts ahead to choose a route.
games.why: they stayed as long as the cloud rested, and traveled when it lifted. and Rashi says even those stops count as journeys.

practice: Ask yourself honestly what tells you when to move and when to stay: a person you trust, a text you return to, a quiet sense in your gut, a tradition, fear sometimes.
Then think of a stop you're in right now, a waiting place that feels like nowhere, and try seeing it the way Rashi reads the verse: part of the journey, not a break from it.
